proofs.proof_tex:
Write the thin singular-value decomposition as
\[
L_n=U_nS_nV_n^{\top}.
\]
Assumption \ref{ass:known-rank} makes the diagonal matrix \(S_n\) invertible. Fix \(b\in\mathcal B_n\). Then
\[
L_{n,C_bP_b}=U_{n,C_b}S_nV_{n,P_b}^{\top}.
\]
The rank hypothesis in the lemma says that the left side has rank \(r\). Since both outer factors have \(r\) columns, it follows that
\[
\operatorname{rank}(U_{n,C_b})=
\operatorname{rank}(V_{n,P_b})=r.
\]
Thus \(U_{n,C_b}^{\top}U_{n,C_b}\) and \(V_{n,P_b}^{\top}V_{n,P_b}\) are invertible. The Moore--Penrose inverse of the displayed full-rank factorization is therefore
\[
L_{n,C_bP_b}^{\dagger}
=V_{n,P_b}(V_{n,P_b}^{\top}V_{n,P_b})^{-1}
S_n^{-1}(U_{n,C_b}^{\top}U_{n,C_b})^{-1}U_{n,C_b}^{\top}.
\]
Direct multiplication, using each inverse only after the preceding rank conclusion, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&L_{n,I_bP_b}L_{n,C_bP_b}^{\dagger}L_{n,C_bQ_b}\\
&\quad=U_{n,I_b}S_nV_{n,P_b}^{\top}
V_{n,P_b}(V_{n,P_b}^{\top}V_{n,P_b})^{-1}
S_n^{-1}(U_{n,C_b}^{\top}U_{n,C_b})^{-1}U_{n,C_b}^{\top}
U_{n,C_b}S_nV_{n,Q_b}^{\top}\\
&\quad=U_{n,I_b}S_nV_{n,Q_b}^{\top}
=L_{n,I_bQ_b}.
\end{aligned}
\]
By the four-block cover in the definition of \(B_n\), the rectangles \(I_b\times P_b\), \(C_b\times P_b\), and \(C_b\times Q_b\) are subsets of \(\Omega_n\). Assumption \ref{ass:treatment-support} and Definition \ref{def:observed-experiment} say that the mean of every such observed block under \(\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\) is the corresponding block of \(L_n\). Hence the right side of the block identity is a functional of the tuple-indexed observed mean. The causal counterfactual remains \(L_{n,I_bQ_b}\); the displayed algebra proves its equality to that observed-law functional rather than defining the counterfactual to be the functional.

Under Definition \ref{def:observed-experiment} and Assumption \ref{ass:treatment-support}, write
\[
X_n=\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)+e_n,
\qquad
e_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|}).
\]
Definition \ref{def:randomized-split} supplies an independent
\(\Xi_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|})\). Therefore
\[
X_n^{(1)}=\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)+e_n+\Xi_n,
\qquad
X_n^{(2)}=\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)+e_n-\Xi_n.
\]
Both centered errors are Gaussian with covariance \(2\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|}\), while their cross-covariance is
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(e_n+\Xi_n,e_n-\Xi_n)
=\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|}-\sigma^2I_{|\Omega_n|}=0.
\]
The pair is jointly Gaussian because it is a linear image of the jointly Gaussian vector \((e_n,\Xi_n)\). Zero cross-covariance therefore gives independence, proving the assertion.

Put \(m=n/2\). In the singleton chart, \(C=C_{b_0}\), \(I=I_{b_0}\), \(P=P_{b_0}\), and \(Q=Q_{b_0}\) all have cardinality \(m\), while \(C_{0,n}=C\) and \(P_{0,n}=P\). Definition \ref{def:chart-graph} therefore sets both synchronization rotations to the identity, and Definition \ref{def:synchronized-pilot} sets \(a_{\mathrm{sync},n}=1\).

Let
\[
B=L_{n,CP}=U_{n,C}S_nV_{n,P}^{\top}.
\]
Assumption \ref{ass:overlap-grams} and \(N_n=T_n=n\) imply
\[
\lVert U_{n,C}x\rVert_2^2\ge\frac{\kappa}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2,
\qquad
\lVert V_{n,P}x\rVert_2^2\ge\frac{\kappa}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2.
\]
Since \(r=1\), Assumption \ref{ass:strong-factors} consequently yields
\[
s_1(B)\ge\frac{\kappa s_-n}{2}=:\delta_0,
\qquad
\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\lVert L_{n,A}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le s_+n=:M_0.
\]
There are at most three distinct rectangles in \(\mathcal A_n\), and each side length is at most \(n\). Hence Definition \ref{def:synchronized-pilot} gives
\[
\varepsilon_n
\le\sqrt2\sigma\left(2\sqrt n+\sqrt{2\log(16/\alpha)}\right)
=O(\sigma\sqrt n).
\]
Thus, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\varepsilon_n\le\delta_0/16\).

We record the deterministic rank-one perturbation calculation used at every stage. If \(B_0=suv^{\top}\), \(\lVert u\rVert_2=\lVert v\rVert_2=1\), \(s\ge\delta_0\), and \(\lVert E\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_n\le\delta_0/16\), then, after putting the leading singular triplet \((\widehat u,\widehat s,\widehat v)\) in the population anchor gauge,
\[
|\widehat s-s|\le\varepsilon_n,
\qquad
\lVert(I-uu^{\top})\widehat u\rVert_2
\le\frac{2\varepsilon_n}{\delta_0},
\qquad
\lVert(I-vv^{\top})\widehat v\rVert_2
\le\frac{2\varepsilon_n}{\delta_0}.
\]
The first inequality follows from the variational definitions of the largest singular value. Projecting \((B_0+E)\widehat v=\widehat s\widehat u\) onto \(u^{\perp}\) gives
\[
\widehat s\lVert(I-uu^{\top})\widehat u\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_n.
\]
Since \(\widehat s\ge s-\varepsilon_n\ge15\delta_0/16\), the asserted left-vector bound follows, and the right-vector bound follows symmetrically.

In the balanced singular-value gauge, every first anchor regression is a product
\[
\frac{A\widehat v}{\sqrt{\widehat s}}
=A(\widehat v\sqrt{\widehat s})(\widehat s)^{-1},
\]
or its transpose. Adding and subtracting \(A_0v/\sqrt s\), using the preceding bounds, \(\lVert A-A_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_n\), and \(\lVert A_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le M_0\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\lVert\frac{A\widehat v}{\sqrt{\widehat s}}
-\frac{A_0v}{\sqrt s}\right\rVert_2
&\le
\frac{\varepsilon_n}{\sqrt{\widehat s}}
+\frac{M_0\lVert\widehat v-v\rVert_2}{\sqrt{\widehat s}}
+M_0\left|\widehat s^{-1/2}-s^{-1/2}\right|\\
&\le16(1+M_0/\delta_0)^2
\frac{\varepsilon_n}{\sqrt{\delta_0}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The square-root difference in the last line uses
\[
|\widehat s^{-1/2}-s^{-1/2}|
=\frac{|\widehat s-s|}
{\sqrt{\widehat s}\sqrt s(\sqrt{\widehat s}+\sqrt s)}
\le\frac{\varepsilon_n}{\delta_0^{3/2}}.
\]
Repeating the same add-and-subtract calculation for the refinement step, and then using
\[
\lVert\widehat f\widehat g^{\top}-fg^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\lVert\widehat f-f\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2
+\lVert f\rVert_2\lVert\widehat g-g\rVert_2
+\lVert\widehat f-f\rVert_2\lVert\widehat g-g\rVert_2,
\]
shows that every fitted block has error at most
\[
2048\left(1+\frac{M_0}{\delta_0}\right)^4\varepsilon_n
\le4096\left(1+\frac{2s_+}{\kappa s_-}\right)^4\varepsilon_n
=\tau_n.
\]
There is only one representation of each row and column, so deterministic aggregation introduces no further amplification. On \(\mathcal G_n\), all input perturbations used above are bounded by their \(\varepsilon_A\), hence by \(\varepsilon_n\). This proves the simultaneous envelope and, by the displayed deterministic bound on \(\varepsilon_n\), its \(O(\sigma\sqrt n)\) order.

Put \(m=n/2\), and abbreviate
\[
\delta_0=\frac{\kappa s_-n}{2},
\qquad
M_0=s_+n,
\qquad
\chi=1+\frac{s_+}{\kappa s_-}.
\]
The balanced rectangle collection has at most three distinct rectangles. For an \(a\)-by-\(b\) matrix \(G\) with independent \(\mathcal N(0,2\sigma^2)\) entries, the Gaussian moment-generating-function bound applied to the variational formula for \(\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) gives
\[
\Pr\left\{\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>
\sqrt2\sigma(\sqrt a+\sqrt b+t)\right\}\le e^{-t^2/2}.
\]
With the threshold in Definition \ref{def:synchronized-pilot} and a union bound,
\[
\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\Pr(\mathcal G_n^c)
\le\frac{3\alpha}{16}<\frac{\alpha}{4}.
\]
The same inequality evaluated at \(t\asymp\delta_0/\sigma\), together with \(\varepsilon_n=O(\sigma\sqrt n)\), yields, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\Pr(\mathcal F_n)
\le C_1\exp\{-c_1s_-^2n/\sigma^2\}.
\]
Here \(c_1\) absorbs the fixed \(\kappa\); the displayed exponent is weaker than the direct order-\(n^2\) exponent and is therefore valid. Since an exponential dominates \(n^{-1}\), after increasing the threshold in \(n\),
\[
\Pr(\mathcal F_n)\le C_2\frac{\sigma}{s_+n},
\qquad
s_+n^{3/2}\Pr(\mathcal F_n)\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.
\]

We next audit the conditional Gaussian term. Let
\[
\mathcal H_n=
\left\{\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}
\lVert(X_n^{(1)})_A-L_{n,A}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\delta_0/4\right\}.
\]
On the stable branch, the derivative of \(f(A,B,C)=AB^{\dagger}C\) is the sum of the three displayed derivative terms in Definition \ref{def:transport-map}. In rank one, each term has rank at most one, so their sum has rank at most three. The overlap inequalities, stability, and the perturbation calculation in Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-sync-envelope} give
\[
\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\le Cn,
\qquad
\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\ell_2\to F}\le C
\]
on \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), where the constants depend only on \(\kappa,s_-,s_+\). For example, the \(H_1\) term has Hilbert--Schmidt norm squared
\[
m\lVert B^{\dagger}C\rVert_F^2\le Cm;
\]
the \(H_3\) term is symmetric. The \(H_2\) term is bounded by inserting
\[
\lVert B^{\dagger}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le C/n,
\qquad
\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\lVert C\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le Cn
\]
in the three summands of \(D(B^{\dagger})\). The same bounds hold for the plug-in matrices on \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\).

On \(\mathcal H_n^c\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), the same derivative formula, now using only \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\), gives the deterministic polynomial envelope
\[
\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}
\le C\sqrt n\left(1+\frac{\widehat M_n}{\tau_n}\right)^2,
\qquad
\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\ell_2\to F}
\le C\left(1+\frac{\widehat M_n}{\tau_n}\right)^2.
\]
The Gaussian operator-norm tail preceding the definition of \(\mathcal H_n\), integrated against this polynomial, implies
\[
\mathbb E\left[
\left\{\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}
+\sqrt{\log K_n}\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\ell_2\to F}\right\}
\mathbf 1_{\mathcal H_n^c\cap\mathcal F_n^c}\right]
\le C\sqrt n.
\]
Indeed, \(\widehat M_n\) is bounded by \(M_0+\varepsilon_n\) plus the same maximum Gaussian operator norm, whereas
\(\Pr(\mathcal H_n^c)\le C\exp(-cs_-^2n^2/\sigma^2)\); every fixed polynomial moment is therefore absorbed by that exponential.

If \(Z_n=\operatorname{mat}_{W_n}(\widehat\Sigma_n^{1/2}Z)\), then conditionally on the pilot,
\[
\mathbb E(\lVert Z_n\rVert_*\mid X_n^{(1)})
\le\sqrt3\,\mathbb E(\lVert Z_n\rVert_F\mid X_n^{(1)})
\le\sqrt6\,\sigma\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}}
\le C\sigma\sqrt n
\]
on \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\). Markov's inequality at conditional probability \(\alpha/4\), the polynomial-tail integral on \(\mathcal H_n^c\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), and the convention \(\mathring q_{\alpha,n}=0\) on \(\mathcal F_n\) give
\[
\mathring q_{\alpha,n}
\le\frac4\alpha\mathbb E(\lVert Z_n\rVert_*\mid X_n^{(1)}),
\qquad
\mathbb E\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\le C_1\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
Moreover, on \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), \(\lVert Z_n\rVert_*\), as a function of the underlying standard Gaussian vector, is \(C\sigma\)-Lipschitz because its matrix rank is at most three and \(\lVert\widehat J_n\rVert_{\ell_2\to F}\le C\). Integrating the elementary Gaussian tail bound there, using the preceding polynomial-tail integral on \(\mathcal H_n^c\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), and using \(\log K_n=O(\log\log n+\log\alpha^{-1})\), gives
\[
\mathbb E\left[
\max_{1\le k\le K_n}T_k\,\mathbf 1_{\mathcal F_n^c}\right]
\le C\sigma\{\sqrt n+\sqrt{\log K_n}\}
\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
Here the maximum is read as zero on \(\mathcal F_n\), consistently with the fallback convention. Since \(0\le\widehat q_{\alpha,n}\le\max_kT_k\),
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat q_{\alpha,n}-\mathring q_{\alpha,n})_+]
\le C_1\sigma\sqrt n,
\qquad
\mathbb E\widehat q_{\alpha,n}\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.
\]

On \(\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), Weyl's inequality and the population bounds give
\[
c\,s_-n\le\widehat\delta_n\le C\,s_+n,
\qquad
\widehat M_n\le C\,s_+n.
\]
The synchronization envelope obeys \(\tau_n\le C\chi^4\sigma\sqrt n\). Substitution into the homogeneous formula, with \(r=1\), yields term by term
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr R_n^{(2)}
&=C_0\tau_n^2
\left\{\widehat\delta_n^{-1}
+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}
+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3}\right\}\\
&\le C\sigma^2n\left\{\frac1{s_-n}
+\frac{s_+n}{s_-^2n^2}
+\frac{s_+^2n^2}{s_-^3n^3}\right\}\\
&\le C_2\frac{\sigma^2}{s_-}
\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n
\end{aligned}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). The same \(\widehat\delta_n\) and \(\widehat M_n\) orders hold throughout \(\mathcal H_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), whether or not the sharper event \(\mathcal G_n\) occurs. On \(\mathcal H_n^c\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), stability still gives \(\widehat\delta_n\ge4\tau_n\), while
\[
\widehat M_n\le M_0+
\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\lVert(X_n^{(1)})_A-L_{n,A}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\varepsilon_n.
\]
Integrating the preceding Gaussian tail after the large-gap cutoff bounds the expectation of \(\tau_n+\widehat M_n+\widehat M_n^2/\tau_n\) on that event by \(C\sigma\sqrt n\). Consequently
\[
\mathbb E[\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\mathbf 1\{\mathcal F_n^c\}]
\le C_2\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
Thus the Gaussian quantile, finite simulation, homogeneous remainder, and fallback are controlled separately, as claimed.

On the stable branch, Lemma \ref{lem:block-transport} gives
\[
\operatorname{vec}_{W_n}(L_n)
=F_n(\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)).
\]
Let \(\ell_n=\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L_n)\) and \(\widetilde\ell_n=\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(\widetilde X_n)\). From Definition \ref{def:wedge-spectral-procedure},
\[
\operatorname{vec}_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)
=\widehat J_n(X_n^{(2)}-\ell_n)
+\{F_n(\widetilde\ell_n)-F_n(\ell_n)
-\widehat J_n(\widetilde\ell_n-\ell_n)\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal F_n^c\), Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-sync-envelope} bounds every argument perturbation by \(\tau_n\), and stability places every intervening anchor singular value above \(\widehat\delta_n/2\). Expanding each occurrence of the inverse by
\[
(B+H)^{-1}-B^{-1}=-B^{-1}H(B+H)^{-1}
\]
on the rank-one row and column spaces, and bounding the three possible placements of two perturbations, gives
\[
\left\lVert
F_n(\widetilde\ell_n)-F_n(\ell_n)
-\widehat J_n(\widetilde\ell_n-\ell_n)
\right\rVert_*
\le C_0\tau_n^2
\left(\widehat\delta_n^{-1}
+\widehat M_n\widehat\delta_n^{-2}
+\widehat M_n^2\widehat\delta_n^{-3}\right)
=\mathscr R_n^{(2)}.
\]
No division occurs before the stable lower bound \(\widehat\delta_n>0\) is invoked.

By Lemma \ref{lem:randomized-split-law}, conditionally on \(X_n^{(1)}\),
\[
\widehat J_n(X_n^{(2)}-\ell_n)
\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n).
\]
It therefore has nuclear norm at most \(\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\) with conditional probability at least \(1-\alpha/4\). Conditional on the pilot, put
\[
B_k=\mathbf 1\{T_k<\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\}.
\]
By the definition of the left \(1-\alpha/4\) quantile, \(\mathbb E(B_k\mid X_n^{(1)})\le1-\alpha/4\). Applying exponential Markov inequality to the product Bernoulli moment-generating function and optimizing over its positive argument gives
\[
\Pr\left\{K_n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}B_k>
1-\alpha/4+\eta_n
\ \middle|\ X_n^{(1)}\right\}
\le e^{-2K_n\eta_n^2}
=\frac{\alpha}{8n}.
\]
On its complement, fewer than \(K_np_n\) simulated values are strictly below \(\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\), so the definition of \(p_n\) ensures \(\widehat q_{\alpha,n}\ge\mathring q_{\alpha,n}\). The balanced Gaussian rectangle bound in Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-radius-audit} gives \(\Pr(\mathcal G_n^c)<\alpha/4\). A union bound, using \(n\ge2\), shows that on the stable branch the nuclear ball fails with probability at most
\[
\frac\alpha4+\frac\alpha4+\frac\alpha{16}<\alpha.
\]
On the fallback branch,
\[
\lVert P_{W_n}L_n\rVert_*
\le\lVert L_n\rVert_*
\le r s_+\sqrt{N_nT_n}
\le s_+\sqrt{r\min\{N_n,T_n\}N_nT_n},
\]
where the last inequality uses \(r\le\min\{N_n,T_n\}\). Since the fallback center is zero, coverage there is deterministic. This proves
\[
(\widehat L_n,\widehat R_{\alpha,n})\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}.
\]

Lemma \ref{lem:total-wsvd} gives randomized polynomial time. Finally, Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-radius-audit} and the fallback identities \(N_n=T_n=n\) and \(r=1\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\mathbb E\widehat R_{\alpha,n}
&\le
\sup_{\vartheta_n}\mathbb E[
\widehat q_{\alpha,n}\mathbf 1_{\mathcal F_n^c}]
+\sup_{\vartheta_n}\mathbb E[
\mathscr R_n^{(2)}\mathbf 1_{\mathcal F_n^c}]
+s_+n^{3/2}\sup_{\vartheta_n}\Pr(\mathcal F_n)\\
&\le C\sigma\sqrt n.
\end{aligned}
\]

The upper bound follows immediately from Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-wsvd-certificate} and Definition \ref{def:minimax-radius}:
\[
\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}
\le\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}
[\widehat R_{\alpha,n}]
\le C\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
We prove the all-procedure lower bound directly. Put \(m=n/2\), let \(C=P=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(I=Q=\{m+1,\ldots,n\}\), and set \(v=n^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_n\). Choose \(s_0\in[s_-,s_+]\), which is possible because \(s_-\le s_+\), and let \(d=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\). Select orthonormal vectors
\[
w_j=2^{-1/2}(e_{m+2j-1}-e_{m+2j}),
\qquad 1\le j\le d.
\]
They are supported on \(I\) and orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1_I\). Fix \(\lambda>0\), put
\[
\beta=\frac{\sqrt2\lambda\sigma}{s_0n},
\qquad
a=\{1-2d\beta^2\}^{1/2},
\]
and, for \(\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_d)\in\{-1,1\}^d\), define
\[
u_C^\epsilon=n^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_C,
\qquad
u_I^\epsilon=a\,n^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_I
+\beta\sum_{j=1}^d\epsilon_jw_j,
\qquad
L^\epsilon=s_0n\,u^\epsilon v^{\top},
\qquad
D^\epsilon=0.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(2d\beta^2<1\), so \(a\) is real. Orthogonality gives
\[
\lVert u^\epsilon\rVert_2^2
=\frac12+\frac{a^2}{2}+d\beta^2=1.
\]
Hence \(L^\epsilon\) has rank one and singular value \(s_0n\). Moreover,
\[
2\lVert u_C^\epsilon\rVert_2^2=1,
\qquad
2\lVert v_P\rVert_2^2=1,
\]
so both overlap Grams equal one and satisfy every \(0<\kappa\le1\). Since \(\sqrt n\,\beta=O(n^{-1/2})\) and \(a\to1\),
\[
n\max_i|u_i^\epsilon|^2\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
n\max_t|v_t|^2=1
\]
uniformly in \(\epsilon\). The strict inequality \(\mu>1\) therefore gives incoherence for all sufficiently large \(n\). Treatment support is immediate from \(D^\epsilon=0\), so every \(\vartheta^\epsilon=(L^\epsilon,D^\epsilon)\) belongs to \(\Theta_n\).

Only the observed block \(I\times P\) depends on \(\epsilon\). For
\[
H_j=w_j(v_P/\lVert v_P\rVert_2)^{\top},
\]
the matrices \(H_j\) are orthonormal in Frobenius inner product, and the Gaussian projections satisfy
\[
Z_j=\langle H_j,X_{IP}\rangle
=\lambda\sigma\epsilon_j+\sigma\xi_j,
\qquad
\xi_j\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
All remaining observed Gaussian coordinates are independent of \(\epsilon\). Under the uniform prior on the hypercube, the posterior bits therefore factor, and the optimal bit decision is \(\operatorname{sign}(Z_j)\), with independent error probability
\[
p=\Phi(-\lambda)>0.
\]
For any possibly randomized decoder \(\widetilde\epsilon\), the posterior mass of a Hamming ball is maximized by centering it at the coordinatewise posterior mode. Consequently, for every \(0<\delta<p\),
\[
2^{-d}\sum_\epsilon
\Pr_\epsilon\{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)\le\delta d\}
\le\Pr\{\operatorname{Bin}(d,p)\le\delta d\}
\le\exp\{-2d(p-\delta)^2\}.
\]
The last inequality follows by applying exponential Markov inequality to the product Bernoulli moment-generating function and optimizing its argument.

Now take an arbitrary \((\widehat L_n,R_n)\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\). From its center define \(\widetilde\epsilon_j\) by the sign of the coefficient along \(w_j(v_Q/\lVert v_Q\rVert_2)^{\top}\), after subtracting the common component; break zero ties lexicographically. If this sign is wrong, that coefficient differs from its true value by at least \(\lambda\sigma\). Since Frobenius norm is bounded by nuclear norm and these directions are Frobenius-orthonormal,
\[
\lVert P_W(\widehat L_n-L^\epsilon)\rVert_*
\ge\lambda\sigma\sqrt{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)}.
\]
Put \(\delta=p/2\) and \(r_n=\lambda\sigma\sqrt{\delta d}\). Uniform honesty implies
\[
\Pr_\epsilon\{d_H(\widetilde\epsilon,\epsilon)\le\delta d\}
\ge1-\alpha-\Pr_\epsilon\{R_n\ge r_n\}.
\]
Averaging this inequality over \(\epsilon\) and using the preceding binomial bound shows, for all sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
2^{-d}\sum_\epsilon\Pr_\epsilon\{R_n\ge r_n\}
\ge1-\alpha-e^{-dp^2/2}\ge\frac12.
\]
Thus some admissible \(\epsilon\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_\epsilon R_n\ge\frac{r_n}{2}
\ge c\sigma\sqrt n.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\Theta_n\), and then the infimum over every uniformly honest procedure, proves the lower bound. The construction uses only the observed-law family; the arbitrary treatment-effect component is fixed at zero and is never conflated with the missing counterfactual.

Because \(P_{W_n}A_n=A_n\) and \(Y_n=L_n+D_n+E_n\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau_{A,n}-\tau_{A,n}
&=\langle A_n,P_{W_n}(Y_n-\widehat L_n)\rangle
-\langle A_n,D_n\rangle\\
&=\langle A_n,P_{W_n}(L_n-\widehat L_n)\rangle
+\langle A_n,P_{W_n}E_n\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\]
Nuclear--operator duality gives
\[
|\langle A_n,P_{W_n}(L_n-\widehat L_n)\rangle|
\le\lVert A_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*.
\]
Apply Lemma \ref{lem:balanced-wsvd-certificate} with miscoverage level \(\alpha/2\), which is admissible because \(0<\alpha/2<1/4\). Its honesty event
\[
\mathcal E_L=
\{\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*
\le\widehat R_{\alpha/2,n}\}
\]
has probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\). Assumption \ref{ass:gaussian-cells} makes the cell errors on \(W_n\) independent of the observed coordinates on \(\Omega_n\), and
\[
\langle A_n,P_{W_n}E_n\rangle
\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2\lVert A_n\rVert_F^2).
\]
Therefore the two-sided Gaussian event
\[
\mathcal E_E=
\{|\langle A_n,P_{W_n}E_n\rangle|
\le z_{1-\alpha/4}\sigma\lVert A_n\rVert_F\}
\]
has probability \(1-\alpha/2\). A union bound gives
\(\Pr(\mathcal E_L\cap\mathcal E_E)\ge1-\alpha\). On this intersection, the two preceding inequalities are exactly the membership inequality \(\tau_{A,n}\in\mathrm{CI}_{A,n}\). Finally, Assumption \ref{ass:att-diffuse} gives \(\lVert A_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le a_n\), hence the asserted half-length bound. Treated support is used in the algebra; normalization and nonnegativity give the ATT interpretation but are not needed for the coverage inequality. No optimal-length conclusion is drawn.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A single all-procedure lower comparison and randomized polynomial-time upper certificate, both uniform over every admissible deterministic staircase wedge and both matching the wedge tangent modulus up to constants.
open_obligations.obstruction: Quantitative overlap of each observed chart does not itself provide a common anchor, a spectral gap for the chart connection graph, or bounded chart incidence. The available block identity is chartwise, but it does not control the conditioning accumulated when incompatible local gauges are transported around an arbitrary overlap graph. On the converse side, a tangent perturbation that nearly attains the nuclear modulus need not admit a fixed-rank retraction that preserves every overlap Gram, strong-factor bound, and incoherence bound while retaining both its missing-wedge separation and a small observed Gaussian divergence.
open_obligations.attempted: The constructive route was chartwise spectral truncation followed by orthogonal synchronization and one-step Gaussian correction; without graph-gap and incidence bounds, its propagated operator norm cannot be bounded by the stated modulus. The converse route was the prescribed overlap-aligned Varshamov--Gilbert packing followed by a fixed-rank exponential-map retraction; the chartwise least-Gram directions can conflict on overlaps, so no uniform packing cardinality and separation bound was obtained. The balanced one-chart construction avoids both failures and is proved separately.
open_obligations.partial_result: The balanced rank-one one-block interior is closed by Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier}: for every fixed \(\mu>1\), its minimax expected honest radius is \(\Theta(\sigma\sqrt n)\), with both a total polynomial-time upper certificate and an all-procedure lower bound. Lemma \ref{lem:block-transport} also gives an exact computable completion map on every individually full-rank four-block chart. What remains unproved is a uniform comparison with \(\mathfrak R_n\) for every admissible deterministic staircase without common anchors, graph-gap, or bounded-incidence hypotheses.

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential construction. Their setup imposes low rank on a single untreated-potential-outcome matrix \(M^\star\); it does not jointly model post-treatment observations with that untreated potential outcome. Their four-block SVD estimator has non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds under two-sided observed-subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise, and target-local leverage conditions, and it does not impose this note's global-incoherence condition. Accordingly, only the converse comparison transfers upward through the balanced rank-one subclass explicitly embedded here; the constructive nuclear-radius bounds remain specific to this note's class. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply a testing reduction for honest nuclear confidence diameter, but their experiment is isotropic Gaussian trace regression and their central obstruction is rank adaptation. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals and phase transitions for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block; their loss and procedure-specific target differ from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan provide debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions but report no global honest matrix radius. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas its boundary companion shows that the interior rate and unrestricted tangent-modulus comparison do not extend to \(\mu=1\). Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng are functional-specific benchmarks for weighted effects; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
